description: Rust extraction-fidelity corpus. Ground truth is Rust's own parser (see oracle/), so every target must be a crate that `syn::parse_file` accepts.

pinning.policy: Pinned by upstream COMMIT SHA, not by toolchain version. Racket's corpus ships with the interpreter so its version identifies the corpus; Rust crates come from git and drift independently of rustc. results.json records the SHA each target was measured at, and run_fidelity.py refuses to publish a reference measured against an unpinned or drifted checkout.
pinning.ceiling: syn PARSES, it does not EXPAND. An item produced by a macro_rules! invocation is invisible to the oracle AND to jCodeMunch, so it is unscored in both directions. This harness cannot make the claim Racket's makes about macro-introduced names -- see README.md.
pinning.sha_integrity: Every sha is validated as 40 lowercase hex before use. The first draft of this file was written through a shell heredoc and one digit arrived as U+096B DEVANAGARI DIGIT FIVE, which is visually identical at small sizes and would have pinned nothing.

targets.stresses: Idiomatic, well-documented application code. Heavy use of items nested inside function bodies via #[cfg] pairs -- pathutil.rs alone defines `imp` eight times that way.
